description: Logical time decomposed. Lamport's happens-before relation. Vector clocks. Version vectors. Hybrid logical clocks. TrueTime. The mechanisms by which distributed systems order events without synchronised wall clocks.

sub_mechanisms.name: happens_before_relation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Lamport 1978. A → B if: same process and A before B; OR A is send and B is receive of same message; OR transitive.
sub_mechanisms.why: Partial order foundational to distributed systems. Concurrent events not ordered by →. Defines what 'before' means without global clock.

sub_mechanisms.name: lamport_clock_rules
sub_mechanisms.definition: On local event: counter++. On send: include counter. On receive: counter = max(local, received) + 1.
sub_mechanisms.why: Implements happens-before: A → B implies LC(A) < LC(B). Cannot detect concurrency: A || B may have LC(A) < LC(B) anyway.

sub_mechanisms.name: vector_clock_per_node
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each node N maintains vector VC. On local event: VC[N]++. On send: include vector. On receive: element-wise max, then VC[N]++.
sub_mechanisms.why: Captures full causal info. VC(A) ≤ VC(B) iff A → B. Incomparable vectors = concurrent. Used in Dynamo, Voldemort. Cost: O(N) size.

sub_mechanisms.name: version_vector
sub_mechanisms.definition: Variant of vector clock for tracking object versions across replicas. Same math, different use.
sub_mechanisms.why: Used in distributed storage for conflict detection. Two writes with incomparable vectors = conflict needing resolution.

sub_mechanisms.name: vector_clock_size_problem
sub_mechanisms.definition: Vector clock size O(N) for N nodes. Grows unboundedly in dynamic memberships.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cassandra's largest practical limitation. Solutions: bounded vectors (drop oldest), dotted version vectors, server-side timestamps.

sub_mechanisms.name: hybrid_logical_clock_HLC
sub_mechanisms.definition: Combines physical time + logical counter. (pt, c) tuple. Bounded drift from physical clock.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lamport unrelated to wall clock. HLC: roughly physical time + tie-breaker. CockroachDB, YugabyteDB use. Pragmatic compromise.

sub_mechanisms.name: TrueTime_API
sub_mechanisms.definition: Spanner: TT.now() returns [earliest, latest]. Uncertainty bounded by GPS + atomic clocks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tight bounds (~7ms uncertainty) → can wait out uncertainty → external consistency. Google's atomic clock + GPS infrastructure in every datacenter.

sub_mechanisms.name: external_consistency
sub_mechanisms.definition: If T1 commits before T2 in real time, T1's effects visible to T2. Stronger than serializability.
sub_mechanisms.why: Spanner's flagship property. Possible because TrueTime bounds. Other systems (CockroachDB) approximate via HLC + larger uncertainty.

sub_mechanisms.name: commit_wait_for_TrueTime
sub_mechanisms.definition: Spanner: commit holds until TT.now().earliest > commit_time. Ensures real-time order.
sub_mechanisms.why: Wait out uncertainty window. ~7ms commit latency added. External consistency guarantee depends on this wait.

sub_mechanisms.name: Lamport_for_simple_ordering
sub_mechanisms.definition: When concurrency detection not needed, Lamport sufficient. Smaller than vector clocks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Used in distributed log ordering (Kafka offsets analogous), some optimistic concurrency. Trade simplicity for lost concurrency info.

sub_mechanisms.name: vector_clock_garbage_collection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Track which entries can be safely dropped. Per-entry causal stability.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without GC, vector grows unboundedly. With: bounded size + correct causal tracking. Complex to implement correctly.

sub_mechanisms.name: interval_tree_clocks
sub_mechanisms.definition: Bounded-size alternative to vector clocks. ID space partitioned + recombined dynamically.
sub_mechanisms.why: Almeida 2008. Solves vector clock growth problem for dynamic systems. Less widely deployed than vector clocks.

derivation_rules.name: logical_time_replaces_unreliable_wall_clock
if: events must be ordered consistently across nodes
then: logical time (Lamport, vector, HLC) is more reliable than wall clock
derivation_rules.why: Wall clocks drift ms; events within window have wrong relative order. Logical time captures causality. Spanner's TrueTime + commit-wait is the exception (atomic clock infrastructure).

derivation_rules.name: vector_clocks_detect_concurrency_Lamport_does_not
if: concurrent updates must be detected (e.g. for conflict resolution)
then: vector clocks are required; Lamport insufficient
derivation_rules.why: Lamport: A || B may have LC(A) < LC(B), looks ordered. Vector clocks: incomparable vectors prove concurrency. Dynamo-style stores need vector clocks for last-write-wins conflict detection.

derivation_rules.name: HLC_balances_physical_and_logical
if: a distributed system needs roughly-physical-time + ordering
derivation_rules.why: Pure logical: no relation to wall clock; can't say 'around 2pm'. Pure physical: unreliable for ordering. HLC: pt-ish for human-readable + logical for correct ordering. CockroachDB foundation.

derivation_rules.name: TrueTime_enables_external_consistency
derivation_rules.why: Wait out uncertainty window: T1's commit time < T2's start time in real time → T2 sees T1's writes. ~7ms commit latency for external consistency. Spanner's unique capability via atomic clocks.

derivation_rules.name: vector_clock_size_limits_membership
if: vector clocks grow with node membership
then: dynamic membership requires bounded variants or GC
derivation_rules.why: Cassandra clusters with 1000s of nodes: full vector impractical. Solutions: ID-based GC, dotted version vectors, server-side timestamps + sloppy consistency. Trade-offs per system.
